title: I made a browser game where frogs worship a dead fish until it becomes a kaiju
author: RigoJMortis
selftext:
A dead fish washes into your cave. Your little frog-fish cult decides it’s a god.

That’s *Glub Almighty*: a text-heavy browser game where you build a religion around whatever washed up nearby, do rituals, recruit believers, raid wrecks, and eventually turn your chosen idol into a giant monster to fight the other gods.

You can worship the fish, but also a boot, a bucket, a kidnapped bard, a suspicious chair, a rock with a face, or the Concept of Tuesday. They all play a little differently and have their own miracles, events, and kaiju forms.

It’s inspired by stuff like *Warsim*: every tide you choose an action, weird consequences pile up, and bad decisions tend to come back later. For example, robbing an adventurer might work great—until they return much stronger and bring friends.

If you beat the other gods, the game keeps going into running an underwater empire: coups, sieges, marriages, rival cults, and eventually a council of gods.

It’s free, all text, and works in a browser on desktop or phone: [Glub Almighty](https://play.fifthdoor.com/play/glub-almighty?referrer=share&via=62TKtQ41IGOC)

I’d especially love feedback on whether the early game makes sense and which idol you end up choosing.
